mutations.because: with the age measured as infinite every cache entry is old, so one written yesterday is planned for deletion. The test plants entries at 29 days and at one hour and asserts plan.expired is empty and kept is 2, so expect(plan.expired).toEqual([]) fails on that assertion line.
command: cache expiry keeps a cache object younger than thirty days

mutations.because: the boundary moves by one millisecond: an entry exactly 30 days old becomes expired. D242 says older than 30 days, so exactly 30 days is young; the test plants one at exactly 30 days and one at 30 days plus a millisecond and asserts only the second is expired.
command: cache expiry treats exactly thirty days as young and thirty days plus one millisecond as old

mutations.because: the shape check dropped: an old stray under the cache prefix (a nested path, an upper-case digest, a .jpg, the folder marker) is planned as an expired entry. command: cache expiry never deletes a key it does not recognise

mutations.because: the dry-run guard removed: expireCache deletes even though apply is false. The test asserts deleted is 0 and the store's key list is byte-for-byte the same after a dry run.

The test plants the same digest in both orgs and asserts the fresh local entry is the one left.
command: cache expiry deletes each entry under its own org
